varieties.title: Varieties
varieties.intro: A variety is a microgreen you grow and sell by the tray. This screen owns the numbers only — what it costs, how long it takes, how much a tray yields. Every word a customer reads about it lives in content/varieties/[key].json.
varieties.introOps: Grow days sets the delivery date an ad-hoc order is promised. Yield per tray is no longer used to price anything, and it is a range rather than one figure — no two cut trays weigh the same — so give the low and high you have actually measured, published so a customer knows roughly what a tray weighs. Both start as estimates, so revisit them after a few sows.
varieties.pickHint: Lowercase letters and hyphens only — radish, red-amaranth, green-amaranth. No numbers or spaces. This names the content file and the page address, so it is an identifier, not a label.
varieties.howTo: Save it here first, then create content/varieties/[key].json for the name and description and drop photos in public/varieties/[key]/. Until that file exists the variety is flagged below and stays off the site.

plans.title: Plans
plans.intro: There are three plans and there will only ever be three: Everyday Essentials, Rare & Exotic and Pick Your Own. They are defined by their content files in content/plans/, so this screen does not create or delete them — it sets what you tune. Price, box weight, order, and which varieties go in each of the four weeks.
plans.introRotation: A month is a rotation, not the same box four times. Week 1 carries the quick crops sown on the first Sunday and week 2 the slower ones sown that same Sunday (SPEC §5.2), so pick each week by grow days — the figure beside every variety in the list.

racks.title: Shelf racks
racks.intro: Racks with a steel shelf plate at every level. A price is calculated from what the rack is made of, never typed in — enter what the vendor charges for a shelf, a foot of angle, a bolt and a bush, and every rack below reprices itself from those figures. Racks made only of slotted angle, with no plates, are on Angle racks.
racks.introLayers: Three layers, and the split is what saves you the recalculation. Rates change often, so they live in one place. Build rules — four legs, eight bolt pairs a shelf, four bushes a rack — barely change. Racks on sale are the combinations you actually offer.
racks.introFrozen: Change a rate and every rack reprices itself immediately — all three ranges, no approval and nothing to accept row by row. A price you type into a rack row below wins until the next rate change, which then overwrites it.
racks.seedBody: Loads the five shelf sizes and the ₹2 bolt and ₹5 bush you were quoted, plus the build rules and the one angle grade — 1.4 mm powder coat at ₹40 a foot, in orange, green and purple. Nothing already entered is overwritten, so this is safe to press twice.
racks.ratesHint: The top row is what parts cost. The rest is how a rack goes together, and only changes if the vendor changes how they supply it. Shelf count is not a setting — a rack has its height in feet, minus one. Saving any of these reprices every rack that uses it straight away — all three ranges, not just this screen. Nothing to approve and nothing to accept row by row.

Editing a plate's price or size reprices every rack built on it at once.

angleRacks.title: Angle racks
angleRacks.intro: Racks built entirely from slotted angle, with no steel shelf plates. Same legs, same bolts and bushes, same heights — the only thing that changes is what a shelf is.
angleRacks.introRule: A shelf level is a rectangle of angle plus one more length down the middle, which braces the span and is where the LED tube mounts. So it is three lengths and two depths: a 4 × 1 ft level takes three 4 ft pieces and two 1 ft pieces, 14 running feet in all.
angleRacks.introShared: Bolt and bush prices, the build counts, the heights you sell, markup and rounding all come from Shelf racks — one set of rates, so a vendor requote is still one edited number. Change any of them and every rack here reprices itself immediately. Shown below, read-only, with a link to where they are changed.

pipeRacks.title: Pipe racks
pipeRacks.intro: Racks built from 1 inch UPVC pipe, joined with four-way connectors. Light to move, nothing to rust, wipes clean — chosen for stability rather than for price, and it is the dearest of the three ranges.
pipeRacks.introRule: A shelf level is a rectangle of pipe — two lengths and two depths, and no middle rail. From 4 ft long it gets a leg under the middle of each long side instead, which is what holds the span up. Every junction takes a four-way connector, and every leg takes a bottom bush.
pipeRacks.introCost: The fittings, not the pipe, set the price. At ₹110 a connector against ₹25 a foot, a 6 ft rack's twenty connectors cost more than all of its pipe put together — so height is expensive here and depth is cheap, because a deeper shelf adds pipe without adding junctions.
pipeRacks.introShared: The four corner legs, the heights you sell, markup and rounding come from Shelf racks — they are the same for every range, and changing them there reprices these racks immediately. The pipe, connector and bush rates are this range's own and are set below, because nothing else buys them.
pipeRacks.ratesHint: The three material rates only this range uses. Everything else is shared, and shown underneath. Saving any of these reprices every rack that uses it straight away — all three ranges, not just this screen. Nothing to approve and nothing to accept row by row.

seeds.title: Seeds
seeds.intro: Seed you hold and sell by the 100 g. This screen owns two numbers only — what 100 g costs, and how many grams are on the shelf. Neither is shown to a customer as a stock figure. Every word a customer reads about a seed lives in content/seeds/[key].json.
seeds.introOps: Stock is a count, not a running total: type what you have just weighed. It is no longer a limit — a customer can order any amount, and this figure decides the promise: up to what you hold goes out next day, beyond it is bought in and promised within 10 days. So a seed at 0 g is still on sale, it just always ships on the vendor run. One order line still caps at 20 packs (2 kg) — more than that is a wholesale conversation. Nothing decrements this figure yet; that arrives with checkout.

trays.title: Trays & drainage
trays.intro: Trays and drainage cells, bought in from a supplier and resold. This screen owns two numbers only — what the pack costs, and how many days it takes to reach a customer. Every word a customer reads about an item lives in content/trays/[key].json.
trays.introOps: Nothing in this category is held in stock, so there is no count to keep and no out-of-stock state: every order is a purchase order placed with the supplier. That is why the lead time matters more here than the price — it is the promise on the card, and it is set per item because these come from more than one supplier. Seven days is the shortest this category will promise. Trays cannot be added to a cart yet; the page lists them and states the wait.

settings.title: Product visibility
settings.intro: Turn a product type off to pull it from every menu on the site — the header, the footer and the shop's own category strip — and take its pages down. A visitor with an old link or a bookmark is sent back to /shop instead of an error. Nothing is deleted: prices, stock and content files are untouched, and turning it back on restores it exactly as it was.

orders.title: Orders
orders.intro: Needs attention is every order still in your hands. Mark one picked when you start putting it together, ready for delivery when it is complete, and handed over when the delivery agent takes it. Unpaid checkouts are not orders — look there only when a customer says they paid and has no receipt.

delivery.title: Delivery
delivery.intro: Orders with microgreens go on your own same-day run and pay the fixed fee below. Every other order pays the courier's live price, quoted at checkout from the pickup address to the customer's PIN for the parcel weight worked out from the packing figures. Subscriptions pay no delivery. Until this is saved (and, for courier orders, the courier is connected), checkout shows no price and does not take payment.

delivery.greensHint: A fixed fee for any order with microgreens in it, whatever else rides along — they go on your own same-day run, not by courier. Set it from your average cost per drop and review it monthly.
delivery.packingHint: Order-wide figures for courier orders. Each tray's size and weight is set on its row in Trays & drainage. Racks pack two ways: a shelf rack is a stack of plates, each adding its plate's packed thickness (Shelf racks → plates); an angle or pipe rack is a bundle of legs and rails, measured by the angle's width and stacking (Shelf racks → angle rates) or the pipe's diameter (Pipe racks → rates). Grams per shelf is on each plate, frame and pipe size. Seeds are weighed by what's ordered, in 5 × 5 × 5 cm packets per 100 g.

field.seedPackingGrams: Seed box and padding, per order (g)

delivery.saved: Saved. Checkout uses these figures from now on.

statusOtherOff.ekart: Ekart is not connected. Set EKART_CLIENT_ID, EKART_USERNAME and EKART_PASSWORD to add it to the checkout comparison.
statusOtherOff.shiprocket: Shiprocket is not connected. Set SHIPROCKET_EMAIL and SHIPROCKET_PASSWORD (the API user, not the account login) to add it to the checkout comparison.

delivery.statusOtherNoSettings: {courier} is connected. Save the pickup address below to start quoting.
delivery.statusOtherOk: {courier} is working: 500 g within {pincode} quotes from ₹{price, number} ({count, plural, one {# option} other {# options}}).
delivery.anglePacking: slotted angle width and stacking, in the angle rates on Shelf racks
delivery.pipePacking: pipe outer diameter, in the pipe rates

checkoutDelivery.notConfigured: Only you see this. No delivery fee is saved yet, so checkout can't price delivery. Customers see "not available right now" and can't pay.
checkoutDelivery.noCourier: Only you see this. Nothing in this cart is microgreens, so it goes by courier — and no courier is connected (set DELHIVERY_API_TOKEN, the EKART_ variables or the SHIPROCKET_ variables). Customers see "not available right now" and can't pay.
checkoutDelivery.notMeasured: Only you see this. An item in this cart has no packing measurements, so the courier can't price the parcel. Delivery settings lists which item and where to add them.
